name: Willem die Madocke maecte
bio: Willem die Madocke maecte ("Willem who made Madoc") is the name the poet gives himself in the opening line of Van den vos Reynaerde, the oldest surviving Middle Dutch beast epic. Nothing else is known of him; the poem is generally dated to the middle of the thirteenth century and placed in Flanders.

His Reynaerde is a free adaptation of French fox stories from the Roman de Renart cycle, and a later version by another poet, Reynaerts historie, is based on it. Willem's own text survives in the Comburg manuscript and in the Darmstadt fragment; the Dyck manuscript preserves a variant text.
